newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly lower on Monday after spending most of the session with larger losses.

Dealers said the local market was stuck in the doldrums, with many investors off on holiday and others unwilling to commit to the market due to currency and rate worries and a slew of important U.S. figures out later this week.

The continued strength of the dollar against the mark and guilder again kept the Dutch curve in flattening mode through the day and with Bund futures languishing, the market was unable to get up any steam at all, one said.

Guilders again lagged Bunds on the spreads. Some analysts see the narrowing of the yield discount to Germany as an established trend, arguing that only a Dutch rate hike, in focus due to the weak guilder, would reverse the process.

But others feel a hike is not that likely, arguing there is no fundamental economic argument for a credit tightening and any rate rise to defend the guilder would be self defeating due to the negative impact on the bond market.
The very long end of the Dutch curve was again under pressure, with some signs of switching out of 30-year paper, a broker said.
The 2-10 year spread on the Dutch yield curve touched lows of 157 basis points on Monday, down from 193 just a month ago.
The sharp decline in the guilder and the worries about short-term interest rates would keep the curve under pressure, traders said.
